claims.text: Economic factors, trust, religious beliefs, and close others' advice dominate patients' reasons for choosing traditional bonesetters.
claims.quote: The results of the analysis of 4 articles found that the reasons for choosing TBS in the case of fracture were dominated by economic factors, trust in TBS, religious beliefs, and advice from people closest to them.

claims.text: Education and integration of traditional with modern medicine are recommended to reduce fracture-related morbidity and mortality.
claims.quote: Therefore, it is recommended to increase educational efforts and integrate traditional medicine with modern medicine to reduce the incidence of morbidity and mortality.

claims.text: Male and female prison peer caregivers differ in motivation, with males emphasizing identity, masculinity, and religion and females meaningful relationships.
claims.quote: While male peer caregivers in the sample appeared to be motivated by issues related to identity, masculinity and religious beliefs, female peer caregivers cited the value of meaningful relationships.

claims.text: Both groups shared daily experiences and learning needs and received intrinsic and extrinsic rewards from caregiving.
claims.quote: However, there were several similarities between male and female's daily experiences and learning needs, and both groups enjoyed intrinsic and extrinsic rewards associated with their roles.

claims.text: Research and policies should clarify peer-caregiving benefits and increase training for caregivers and correctional staff.
claims.quote: Findings underscore the need for more research aimed at making explicit the varying benefits of peer caregiving behind bars, as well as policies ensuring increased training for peer caregivers and correctional staff.

claims.text: Religiosity remains a dominant influence on contemporary Indonesian baby naming.
claims.quote: First, religiosity remains a dominant influence, reflected in the frequent use of Arabic-derived names and names carrying religious meanings.

claims.text: Globalization significantly shapes naming patterns through multilingual elements.
claims.quote: Second, globalization has significantly shaped naming patterns, as evidenced by the incorporation of linguistic elements from various languages, including English, French, Hebrew, and Sanskrit, often combined within a single name.

claims.text: Baby names represent cultural values, religious beliefs, aspirations, and global orientations as well as identity.
claims.quote: These findings suggest that baby names function not only as markers of personal identity but also as representations of cultural values, religious beliefs, social aspirations, and contemporary global orientations.

claims.text: Greater religious influence correlates with a broader range of faith-based and secular coping strategies.
claims.quote: Higher religious influence correlated with a broader range of coping strategies, both faith-based (e.g., prayer, church attendance) and secular (e.g., work-related tasks, nature immersion, creative outlets).

claims.text: Religiosity may protect Spanish-speaking patients by expanding stress-coping behaviors.
claims.quote: These findings suggest that religiosity is associated with an expanded breadth of coping behaviors among Spanish-speaking patients and may serve as an additional protective factor in managing stress.

claims.text: Mental-health support should be tailored to individual religiosity and acculturation.
claims.quote: Lastly, this study reiterates the importance of tailoring support to individual levels of religiosity and acculturation.

claims.text: Positive attitudes, knowledge, and personal acquaintance with donors predict willingness to donate organs.
claims.quote: In the full-sample logistic regression (N = 895), positive attitudes (odds ratio [OR] = 5.65, p < 0.001), higher knowledge (OR = 1.56, p < 0.001), and knowing someone who had donated or was considering donating (OR = 1.96, p = 0.013) predicted willingness to donate.

claims.text: Organ-donation willingness remains low despite broadly positive attitudes in China.
claims.quote: Collectively, these findings indicate that organ donation willingness in China remains low despite broadly positive attitudes.

claims.text: Education and institutional transparency are needed because uncertainty and family norms impede commitment.
claims.quote: Knowledge deficits, procedural uncertainty, and family-centered decision-making norms impede commitment, thereby underscoring the need for enhancing public education and institutional transparency.

claims.text: Sacred groves support local ecosystems by protecting species, soil, water, and microclimates.
claims.quote: They have come to play an essential role in local ecosystems due to their protection of indigenous species, maintenance of soil and water, and preservation of microclimatic balance.

claims.text: Urbanization, resource exploitation, declining traditional faiths, climate change, and biomass removal threaten sacred groves.
claims.quote: But these groves are increasingly threatened by various factors such as urbanization, conversion of agricultural land, modernization and market pressure, deforestation, exploitation of resources, and the loss of traditional faiths which once ensured their protection. Climate change coupled with excessive removal of biomass further accelerates the degradation of their ecological integrity.

claims.text: Successful sacred-grove management requires balancing scientific knowledge with indigenous cultural traditions.
claims.quote: Going forward, a balanced approach that respects both scientific knowledge and indigenous cultural traditions is needed for the successful management of sacred trees.

claims.text: Markets depend on informal norms and religious beliefs as well as formal institutions.
claims.quote: Markets depend on both informal institutions (norms and religious beliefs) and formal institutions.

claims.text: Quranic market-conduct verses form a three-tiered institutional structure for permissible and legitimate exchange.
claims.quote: These clusters reflect a three-tiered institutional skeleton: what conditions are required to make an exchange permissible, what integrity requirements help make it work, and the limits defined to explain what makes an exchange legitimate.

claims.text: The paper relates Quranic market-conduct requirements to modern economic concepts.
claims.quote: This paper gives a thematic dataset of Quranic market-conduct requirements and relates them to the modern economic concepts.

claims.text: Political interest can provide purpose while also causing significant stress.
claims.quote: The findings reveal that political interest acts as both a potential source of purpose and a significant stressor.

claims.text: Millennials and Generation Z face heightened anxiety from political polarization and societal pressures.
claims.quote: In contrast, Millennials and Generation Z exhibit a more pragmatic approach, heavily influenced by social media, yet they face heightened anxiety and mental health challenges due to political polarization and societal pressures.

claims.text: Supportive political and social environments are necessary for mental well-being across generations and religions.
claims.quote: Overall, the research underscores the necessity of fostering a supportive political and social environment that promotes mental well-being across diverse generational and religious backgrounds, highlighting the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration between political science and psychology to address these complex issues effectively.

claims.text: Quranic religious tolerance rests on religious freedom, respect for faith differences, and just social relations.
claims.quote: The findings indicate that religious tolerance in the Qur’an is based on three interconnected principles: freedom of religion, respect for differences in faith, and justice and good social relations with others.

claims.text: Islamic tolerance respects differences without mixing beliefs or compromising faith.
claims.quote: These principles demonstrate that tolerance in Islam does not imply mixing religious beliefs or compromising faith, but rather respecting differences while maintaining religious identity and promoting peaceful social relations.

claims.text: Implementing these values in Islamic Religious Education requires contextual, dialogical, and adaptive learning.
claims.quote: However, their implementation requires contextual, dialogical, and adaptive learning approaches to address narrow and exclusive religious interpretations.

claims.text: Christianity reshaped Ibibio socio-cultural life, while Ibibio culture also influenced local Christianity.
claims.quote: The finding revealed how Christianity has influenced and reshaped core aspects of Ibibio socio-cultural life, and on the other hand, how Ibibio culture has influenced the practice of Christianity in the area.

claims.text: Christianity's interaction with Ibibio culture is continuing negotiation that produces inculturation, syncretism, and Africanized Christianity.
claims.quote: The study concluded that the interaction is not of total conflict but of continuous negotiation which prove certain elements of inculturation and syncretism resulting in Africanized Christianity.

claims.text: A balanced inculturation approach should preserve positive Ibibio cultural values while promoting Christian moral principles.
claims.quote: It is strongly recommended that a balanced inculturation approach that preserves positive Ibibio cultural values such as traditional language, arts, music, among others be maintained while promoting Christian moral principles for sustainable development of Ibibioland.

claims.text: Stories of death and the afterlife influence individual conduct, ethical systems, and collective norms across civilizations.
claims.quote: People’s stories of death and the afterlifeinfluence individual conduct, systems of ethics, and collective norms across civilisations, notmerely mirror cultural beliefs.

claims.text: Mythological narratives are enduring structures through which people and societies understand life, death, and moral choices.
claims.quote: Together, these traditions revealthat while religious belief is not the only source of morality, mythological narratives are amongthe most enduring and broad structures that individuals and societies use to make sense of life,death, and the choices in between.

claims.text: Physical disability both excludes elderly beggars from conventional work and increases donations by eliciting sympathy.
claims.quote: The empirical findings indicate that physical disability serves a dual, paradoxical role, it completely bars older individuals from conventional labour markets while functioning as a form of visual capital that increases personal sympathy and material donations from passersby.

claims.text: Karmic and destiny beliefs give suffering meaning but foster fatalism that restricts efforts to escape street dependency.
claims.quote: Entrenched cultural beliefs in past-life karma and destiny provide existential meaning to their current suffering, yet they simultaneously in still a fatalistic framework that restricts their proactive capacity to cope, dampens their courage, and limits their ability to escape chronic street dependency.

claims.text: Physical limitations and internal religious-cultural systems interact to reinforce and normalize chronic socioeconomic marginalization.
claims.quote: This study bridges a vital literature gap by demonstrating how structural physical limitations and internal cultural-religious systems interact to reinforce and normalize chronic socioeconomic marginalization among elderly urban populations.

claims.text: Christianity reshaped core Ibibio social and cultural life, while Ibibio culture also influenced local Christian practice.
claims.quote: The finding revealed how Christianity has influenced and reshaped core aspects of Ibibio socio-cultural life, and on the other hand, how Ibibio culture has influenced the practice of Christianity in the area.

claims.text: Christianity’s encounter with Ibibio culture is ongoing negotiation, producing inculturation, syncretism, and Africanized Christianity rather than total conflict.
claims.quote: The study concluded that the interaction is not of total conflict but of continuous negotiation which prove certain elements of inculturation and syncretism resulting in Africanized Christianity.

claims.text: A balanced inculturation approach should preserve positive Ibibio cultural values while promoting Christian moral principles.
claims.quote: It is strongly recommended that a balanced inculturation approach that preserves positive Ibibio cultural values such as traditional language, arts, music, among others be maintained while promoting Christian moral principles for sustainable development of Ibibioland.

claims.text: The numbers 3, 7, and 40 have shared and divergent symbolic meanings in Kyrgyz and English traditions.
claims.quote: The study reveals that the number 3 in both cultures is associated with completeness and sacred wholeness; however, in the Kyrgyz tradition, three people embody grace and communality, whereas in English usage, the "third wheel" often carries a negative connotation.

claims.text: The number 40 is pervasive in Kyrgyz life rituals but appears rarely in English outside biblical contexts.
claims.quote: The most significant differences are found in the semantics of the number 40: in Kyrgyz culture, it permeates all major life rituals from birth to death, whereas in English, it appears rarely and almost exclusively in biblical contexts.

claims.text: Numerical expressions in proverbs and folklore encode a people’s worldview as cultural codes.
claims.quote: The findings confirm that numbers in proverbs and folklore formulas function as cultural codes encoding the worldview of a people.

claims.text: Religiosity is positively associated with self-reported interpersonal forgiveness across the sampled countries and religious groups.
claims.quote: Results showed that religiosity (i.e., religious belief, bonding, and belonging) was positively associated with self-reported forgiveness.

claims.text: The religiosity-forgiveness association varies by country and religion and is stronger where average religiosity is higher.
claims.quote: This association varied across countries and religious groups and was stronger in countries with higher (vs. lower) average levels of religiosity.

claims.text: Divine love predicts forgiveness only in highly religious countries, while divine punishment predicts less forgiveness especially in less religious countries.
claims.quote: Additionally, experiencing divine love was positively associated with self-reported forgiveness, but only in countries with higher (vs. lower) average levels of religiosity. Conversely, experiencing divine punishment was negatively associated with self-reported forgiveness, which was stronger in countries with lower (vs. higher) average levels of religiosity.

claims.text: Climate variability has significantly disrupted seasonal patterns in Pariangan Village.
claims.quote: Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork involving interviews with 31 participants (each with a minimum of five years of farming experience) and supplemented by climatological data from Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) in 2020–2025, this research identifies significant disruptions to seasonal patterns.

claims.text: Pariangan’s community has developed traditional and collective agricultural adaptations in response to climate disruption.
claims.quote: Consequently, the community has developed adaptation strategies, including village granaries (lumbung nagari), paddy irrigation distribution systems, mixed-garden agroforestry (parak system), mutual cooperation (gotong royong), and belief-based rituals.

claims.text: Policymakers should integrate community environmental knowledge with climate policy and scientific forecasting to strengthen food security and resilience.
claims.quote: To mitigate climate variability and strengthen food security, policymakers must formalize and integrate community-based environmental knowledge into broader climate change adaptation policies and regional development planning.

claims.text: Textbook knowledge is socially constructed through cultural, social, and religious ideological content.
claims.quote: Paper demonstrates the findings which prove that how the textbook knowledge is socially constructed.

claims.text: Pakistani course books serve powerful social groups’ interests while neglecting learners’ interests in syllabus design.
claims.quote: Thus, it has been extracted that course books and textual discourse in Pakistan serves the interests of powerful fraction of society and the interests of learners are kept aside while designing syllabus.

claims.text: Textbooks should transmit knowledge and develop creative, capable learners rather than manipulate young minds.
claims.quote: This paper is to highlight the fact that books must be designed to transmit knowledge, develop creative skills and to make learners capable, therefore they must not be bias and neither should be mean of manipulating young minds

claims.text: Adolescent boys’ menstrual knowledge is fragmented, and misconceptions persist despite information from family, school, and the internet.
claims.quote: Adolescent boys’ knowledge of menstruation was fragmented, stemming from family, school, and internet sources. Mothers were frequently cited as key informants, but misconceptions about menstruation persisted.

claims.text: Sociocultural and religious beliefs reinforce menstrual taboos that shape discriminatory attitudes among adolescent boys.
claims.quote: Sociocultural and religious beliefs reinforced menstruation-related taboos, such as restrictions on cooking and entering sacred spaces, shaping discriminatory attitudes.

claims.text: Inclusive menstrual education for boys and families should address biological, emotional, and social dimensions to reduce myths and foster empathy.
claims.quote: Educational programs should include biological, emotional, and social aspects of menstruation to help reduce myths and nurture empathy.

claims.text: Collective identity powerfully mobilized support and militancy for the Ombatse movement in Nasarawa State.
claims.quote: The paper concludes that collective identity was a powerful mechanism for the mobilisation for support by the Ombatse movement as well as for the deployment of militancy in Nasarawa State.

claims.text: The movement's identity attracted Eggon people by converging with their Christian and Muslim identities.
claims.quote: This identity attracted many Eggon people because it converged with their other identities, including as practicing Christians and Muslims.

claims.text: Widespread support enabled collective action that produced sustained militancy and violent conflict.
claims.quote: The resultant widespread support attracted by the movement enabled it to mobilise its members for collective action in protecting the interests of the Eggon ethnic group. This resulted in their assumption of a sustained militant posture that brought the movement into violent conflicts with other ethnic groups and the Nasarawa State government.

claims.text: Religiosity inclines people toward more cautious and negative euthanasia attitudes, but does not absolutely prevent approval.
claims.quote: Religious attitudes do play a role, inclining believers toward a more cautious and negative attitude toward euthanasia compared to non-believers. However, the high percentage of positive attitudes toward euthanasia among believers suggests that their faith is not an absolute and immutable barrier.

claims.text: Compassion, personal experience, and understanding of suffering influence believers' positive attitudes toward euthanasia.

claims.text: Visible moral patterns, in which outcomes track culpability or desert, are not systematically dominant across history at the aggregate level, so the directional signature c011 describes is absent at the scale history presents.

Robust contrastive responsibility requires that the agent's cognition represent the outcome under an agent-relative aspect (a stance of doing, not merely knowing) that a rigid third-personal identifier cannot supply.

Proper parthood, as used in the divine simplicity claim, is the similarity-relative relation of c018, and that relation tracks metaphysical constituency closely enough that having no proper parts under it expresses the traditional denial of composition.

Schellenberg's analogical route for P1 is successful only if he independently shows that a vulnerable God is obligated to make the beloved's access to relationship available, rather than merely permitted to do so.

Robust contrastive responsibility requires cognition that represents the selected outcome, under the contrast with its alternative, as the result of an act the cognizing agent herself performs and intends, not merely as a state of the world tied to an impersonal lever-state.

Instantiation of God's timelessly and essentially held properties, such as omniscience, can be modelled as parthood because God may be understood as the mereological fusion of those properties, with no claim that this holds for contingent, time-varying properties of ordinary objects.
Multiple goods may arise from a single bounded episode of nonresistant nonbelief, with its evil measured by the lost relationship over that episode rather than by the number of goods it supports.

The analogical route for P1 succeeds only if the features that make Mira's obligation to make access available hold generally in the divine case, namely that God can make access available without cost to the beloved's dignity or safety and that permanent nonresistant nonbelief is not compatible with perfect vulnerable love.

Visible desert-tracking outcomes at the aggregate level are not predicted by either naturalism or theism, so their absence is evidentially neutral between worldviews and c011 cannot serve as an expected-signature premise against theism.

Robust contrastive responsibility requires that the agent's cognition represent the selected outcome, under its contrast with the alternative, as the result of an act the agent herself performs and intends, rather than representing the outcome itself as her action.
For God and each of God's parts, parthood is bivalent, so that God's being part of each such part is settled true rather than merely not false.

Schellenberg's analogical route for P1 is successful only if he independently shows that a vulnerable God is obligated, absent overriding reasons that the hiddenness literature leaves open, to keep voluntary relationship genuinely accessible to the beloved.

Goods individually less valuable than a relationship with God, after subtracting value shared through common dispositional sources, can collectively make a world containing temporary nonresistant nonbelief more valuable than the lost relationship, which is valued for itself.

Robust contrastive responsibility requires that the agent's cognition represent the selected outcome, under the contrast with its alternative, as the result of an act the cognizing agent herself performs and intends, not merely as a state tied to a value-indexed structure.

Multiple goods may arise from a single bounded episode of nonresistant nonbelief without increasing that evil, provided the goods do not require the episode to be lengthened or intensified beyond what the minimal episode supporting them already involves.

For God’s essential attributes, similarity-based parthood is restricted to resemblance relations grounded in metaphysical constituency, so merely qualitative similarity between independently constituted things never suffices for parthood.

The second premise of the expectations sub-argument is false because some person can, by accepting rather than believing that God exists, stand in mutual personal acknowledgment with God, so that belief is unnecessary for explicit, positively meaningful relationship with God.

arguments.title: Divine simplicity as symmetric parthood

atoms.A: God lacks proper parts (the claim taken as the most plausible understanding of divine simplicity)
atoms.C: The symmetry formulation of divine simplicity holds
atoms.D: Instantiation can be modelled as parthood (objects as fusions of their properties)
atoms.E: God and omniscience are mutual parts with respect to similarity while remaining numerically distinct
atoms.F: Proper parthood is defined as non-symmetric similarity-based parthood
atoms.G: Divine simplicity can viably be formulated as the thesis that God is part of all God's parts
atoms.H: Proper parthood is irreflexive, asymmetric, and transitive

arguments.missing_premise: Proper parthood is non-symmetric parthood, and the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity is the thesis that God is part of all God's parts. [B & (C -> G)]

arguments.title: Self-Location Constraint

atoms.A: an agent is robustly contrastively responsible for bringing about one outcome rather than alternatives
atoms.B: the agent's cognition represents the outcome as issuing from its own action or activity
atoms.C: divine cognition represents God as the source of actualising W1 rather than W0
atoms.D: a third-personal proposition identifies God as actualising a world
atoms.E: a proposition represents that actualisation under the first-personal aspect required for source attribution
atoms.F: God is robustly contrastively responsible for actualising W1 rather than W0
atoms.G: God is contrastively responsible for actualising one world rather than another
atoms.H: divine cognition includes irreducible de se content

arguments.missing_premise: God's contrastive responsibility for actualising one world rather than another is robust responsibility, and representing God as the source of that actualisation requires irreducible de se content. [(G -> F) & (C -> H)]

arguments.title: Randomness Underdetermines God
arguments.skeleton: A & B; E; ~F; ~G & B; ~C; H |- D

atoms.A: Apparently random historical events have identifiable biological, political, or social causes
atoms.B: Outcomes of such events appear morally indiscriminate and non-monotonic (suffering appears distributed without visible moral governance)
atoms.C: Scripture promises that moral character determines health, wealth, longevity, or political success in this life
atoms.D: Judging God's existence only by apparent worldly randomness yields no clear winner, because its meaning depends greatly on worldview
atoms.E: Naturalism and biblical theology each explain apparent randomness (naturalism via impersonal causation and probability; biblical theology via agency, natural processes, hidden providence, suffering, and delayed judgment)
atoms.F: Historical evidence has the directional signature expected if history is steered toward the good
atoms.H: Complete justice is located in a future judgment rather than in earthly life

arguments.missing_premise: If rival worldviews each explain apparent randomness and the historical evidence lacks the expected directional signature, then worldly evidence alone cannot decide between them, so judging God's existence by worldly randomness yields no clear winner. [(E & ~F) -> D]

arguments.title: Many-goods response
arguments.skeleton: B -> A; C; D; ~G |- H -> F

atoms.A: A good may overcome the accommodation strategy
atoms.B: Temporary nonresistant nonbelief makes some good sufficiently more valuable
atoms.C: Multiple goods arise from a single instance of nonresistant nonbelief without increasing that evil
atoms.D: Goods individually less valuable than a relationship with God collectively make a world containing nonresistant nonbelief more valuable
atoms.G: Schellenberg's accommodation strategy defeats the many-goods response merely because an individual good can occur within a relationship with God
atoms.H: Every identified good can be realized within a relationship with God

arguments.missing_premise: If every identified good can be realized within a relationship with God, the many-goods conditions still hold, so that multiple goods without increased evil, collectively outweighing goods, and no defeat by the accommodation strategy together make the many-goods response succeed. [H -> ((C & D & ~G) -> F)]

arguments.title: Hiddenness Argument Fails

atoms.A: Schellenberg establishes P1 as an a priori, necessary conceptual truth
atoms.B: Schellenberg's analogical argument for P1 succeeds
atoms.C: The second premise of the expectations sub-argument is true
atoms.E: Belief that God exists is unnecessary for a positively meaningful relationship with God

arguments.missing_premise: Schellenberg's hiddenness argument succeeds only if its conditional premise is established, either by the a priori conceptual route or by the analogical route, and the second premise of the expectations sub-argument is true. [D -> ((A | B) & C)]
